articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 Turbo with Native Multimodal Reasoning Across Audio, Video, and Code
articles.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5 Turbo, featuring deeply integrated multimodal reasoning that can process interleaved video, audio, and code inputs in a single context window of 1M tokens. Benchmarks show a 38% improvement over GPT-5 on complex agentic coding tasks, with substantially reduced hallucination rates. The model is available through the API with a new streaming architecture that cuts time-to-first-token latency by 60%.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves State-of-the-Art on Graduate-Level Scientific Reasoning
articles.summary: DeepMind announced Gemini Ultra 2, which scores 92.4% on the GPQA Diamond benchmark and demonstrates near-expert performance on novel graduate-level physics and biology problems. The model introduces a new 'deliberative alignment' architecture that chains internal verification steps before producing answers. Google has integrated it into Google Cloud's Vertex AI platform with enterprise-grade safety controls.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Begins Limited Deployment in BMW and Amazon Warehouses
articles.summary: Tesla's third-generation Optimus humanoid robot has started operational deployment at select BMW manufacturing plants and Amazon fulfillment centers, performing bin-picking, parts transport, and quality inspection tasks. The Gen 3 units feature 28 degrees of freedom in each hand, a new visual-tactile sensor suite, and can operate autonomously for 14-hour shifts. Tesla reports a 3x improvement in task completion reliability over Gen 2.

articles.title: Figure AI and Microsoft Partner to Build Foundation Model for General-Purpose Humanoid Control
articles.summary: Figure AI announced a partnership with Microsoft Research to develop a large-scale foundation model trained on over 50,000 hours of real-world and simulated humanoid teleoperation data. The model enables zero-shot generalization to novel manipulation tasks, allowing Figure's robots to perform unseen household and industrial tasks after only a natural language instruction. Early demos show the system handling deformable objects and tool use with human-comparable dexterity.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces 'Constitutional Classifiers' as Open-Source Safety Infrastructure
articles.summary: Anthropic open-sourced its Constitutional Classifiers framework, a modular system for detecting and mitigating harmful model outputs using lightweight classifier heads trained via constitutional AI principles. The toolkit allows developers to compose custom safety policies as natural language constitutions and compile them into efficient inference-time guardrails with under 5ms overhead. The release is accompanied by a benchmark suite of 12,000 adversarial red-team scenarios.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm Gate-All-Around Transistor Node
articles.summary: TSMC has commenced high-volume manufacturing on its N1.4 process node at its Kaohsiung fab, utilizing gate-all-around nanosheet transistors with backside power delivery. The node delivers a 25% performance uplift and 35% power reduction over N2, and is expected to power next-generation AI accelerators from Nvidia and Apple in 2027. Yield rates are reportedly exceeding 80%, well ahead of internal targets for this stage of ramp.

articles.title: Meta Debuts Orion AR Glasses for Consumer Pre-Order with Full Holographic Display
articles.summary: Meta opened pre-orders for its Orion AR glasses, featuring a 70-degree field-of-view holographic waveguide display in a form factor weighing 85 grams. The device integrates a custom neural interface wristband for input, runs Meta's Llama 4-powered contextual AI assistant on-device, and supports spatial computing applications. Priced at $1,299, it represents Meta's first mass-market consumer AR product after years of prototype iterations.

articles.title: Startup Extropic Demonstrates First Room-Temperature Thermodynamic Computing Chip for AI Inference
articles.summary: Extropic, a startup founded by former Google quantum computing researchers, publicly demonstrated its first thermodynamic computing processor that performs probabilistic AI inference by harnessing thermal noise in analog circuits at room temperature. The chip achieves energy efficiency of 0.1 picojoules per operation on generative model sampling tasks, roughly 1000x more efficient than equivalent GPU computation. The company raised a $250M Series B to scale production.
